messages:
maria: Hey team — customer (acct: acct_9a2f) reporting repeated 429s during a short traffic spike. They say burst credits show as 0 in headers even though spike was ~45s long. Can someone confirm how burst refill timing works?

josh: Do we have the raw response headers or a snippet of the 429 body? That helps determine whether they hit quota or burst smoothing.

maria: Pasted headers (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1719456840
X-Burst-Credits-Left: 0
X-Burst-Credit-Last-Used: 1719456748
Content-Type: application/json
```
Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","type":"burst_quota"}

sahil: For context — our workload had a 40s ramp (many concurrent short requests) then returned to baseline. They expected burst credits to refill after ~60s but never saw it.

josh: Two quick checks: 1) Is this hosted API or Dedicated? 2) Did they change smoothing policy or have custom quotas?

maria: Hosted API, default smoothing. No custom quotas on the account. Customer says requests are mostly small chat completions (~20 tokens).

josh: Ok. From headers it looks like burst credit counter hit 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset is in ~51s. Burst credit accounting should start refilling immediately after debt is cleared but actual usable credits can be gated by smoothing window. If their traffic pattern is a long sustained ramp (~40s), the smoothing algorithm might consider them part of sustained usage and not grant full immediate refill.

maria: Customer asked for concrete repro steps. Suggested repro:
1) Set up client at 200 req/min baseline for 5m.
2) At t=0 send a 40s spike at 1200 req/min.
3) Observe response headers and X-Burst-Credits-Left.
4) Check for 429s and whether credits go back >0 within 60-90s.

josh: Thanks. I will try to reproduce on staging with same request sizes and concurrency. If we do get consistent 429s after a short spike and credits don't refill as expected, escalate to eng-runtime.

maria: Quick question — is there an admin-visible metric that shows burst-credit balance over time for an account? Customer wants a graph.

josh: Not per-account in Console today — only aggregate metrics and per-route token usage. We can pull per-account burst accounting from internal logs for a support ticket.

sahil: FYI — customer said their product degrades visibly when 429s last >120s. They'd prefer smoothing window tuned toward shorter windows (30–60s) rather than longer.

maria: Workaround offered: throttle client to stay under baseline while spike cooling, or stagger requests to avoid a single simultaneous ramp. Also suggested enabling "burst_smoothing": true in Dedicated config (if they had Dedicated). Not applicable here (hosted).

josh: Repro done on staging — I see the same pattern: burst credits drop to 0 mid-spike and remain at 0 for ~80s, even though refill rate nominally would predict earlier recovery. Logging shows smoothing window sliding incorrectly when ramp is longer than 30s.

maria: Marking this P1 for eng-runtime. Creating internal ticket IR-2026-314 and attaching headers/logs + repro script. Customer updated that they can implement temporary client-side jitter while we investigate.

eng-bot: New internal issue created: IR-2026-314 (eng-runtime) — "Burst smoothing: delayed recovery for mid-length spikes". Priority: P1. Linked: #eng-runtime.

josh: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Patch smoothing function to cap the ramp-detection window at 30s for hosted customers; 2) Roll a canary to 10% in us-west1; 3) Monitor per-account burst balances/429 rate for the canary group.

maria: Notifying customer and asking if they can test again in ~2 hours during canary. cc @sahil — will update ticket with their confirmation.

sahil: Thx — customer ok with canary test. They prefer not to escalate to Dedicated.

maria: Closing loop here once engineering fixes land. For the support doc, I'll add:
- How burst credits are exposed in headers (X-Burst-Credits-Left, X-Burst-Credit-Last-Used)
- Typical refill expectations vs smoothing caveats
- Repro steps + short-term client-side mitigations (jitter/backoff + staggered starts)

josh: Addendum for doc: include example header parsing snippet:```python
import requests
r = requests.get(url, headers=...)
print(r.headers.get('X-Burst-Credits-Left'))
```
maria: Thanks all — updating ticket and will post final resolution in this thread when fix is live. :thumbsup:
